title: Crop Breeding and Genetics
topics: Breeding for disease, pest and stress resistance
Field trials, registration and seed classes
Inheritance of qualitative and quantitative traits
Reproductive systems and their breeding consequences
Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Inbreeding depression may be defined as
o: the extent to which a lot represents the intended constitution without admixture
the deliberate placing of an attacker or its propagules on material being tested
the portion of total variation in a population that is due to differences in constitution
the loss of vigour and fertility that follows repeated mating among close relatives
items.s: Inbreeding depression: the loss of vigour and fertility that follows repeated mating among close relatives. The other options describe Genetic variance, Genetic purity, Inoculation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Vertical resistance?
o: an alteration in the sequence of a single hereditary unit that is passed to later generations
protection that works against some strains of an attacker but not against others
protection spread fairly evenly against every strain of an attacker
the small stock held by the originating institution from which all further multiplication begins
items.s: Vertical resistance: protection that works against some strains of an attacker but not against others. The other options describe Point change, Breeder seed, Horizontal resistance.
items.t: Breeding for disease, pest and stress resistance

items.q: Trait may be defined as
o: a measurable characteristic of an organism such as height, earliness or reaction to an attacker
a hereditary unit moved from one organism into another by artificial means
a feature governed by many hereditary units and expressed as a continuous range of values
the deliberate placing of an attacker or its propagules on material being tested
items.s: Trait: a measurable characteristic of an organism such as height, earliness or reaction to an attacker. The other options describe Inoculation, Transgene, Quantitative character.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: The statement “a hereditary unit moved from one organism into another by artificial means” describes which of the following?
o: Genetic erosion
Regeneration
Transgene
Biosafety
items.s: Transgene is a hereditary unit moved from one organism into another by artificial means.

items.q: The statement “the deliberate placing of an attacker or its propagules on material being tested” describes which of the following?
o: Escape
Vertical resistance
Inoculation
Biotype
items.s: Inoculation is the deliberate placing of an attacker or its propagules on material being tested.
items.t: Breeding for disease, pest and stress resistance

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Genetic purity.
o: the advance of each generation through one propagule per plant until full homozygosity is reached
the extent to which a lot represents the intended constitution without admixture
the masking of the effect of one allele by the other member of the pair at a locus
a feature governed by many hereditary units and expressed as a continuous range of values
items.s: Genetic purity: the extent to which a lot represents the intended constitution without admixture. The other options describe Dominance, Quantitative character, Single seed descent.
items.t: Field trials, registration and seed classes

items.q: Which of the following best describes Genotype?
o: the transfer of male gametes from anther to stigma within the same flower or the same individual
a planting deliberately exposed to heavy attack so that reactions of entries can be compared
the first generation offspring of two inbred parents
the hereditary constitution of an individual, whether considered at one locus or throughout
items.s: Genotype: the hereditary constitution of an individual, whether considered at one locus or throughout. The other options describe Single cross, Self-pollination, Screening nursery.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Wide crossing.
o: the removal of anthers from a flower before they shed so that only a chosen parent fertilises it
the ability to lose less yield than a susceptible plant under the same level of attack
the failure of a plant to shed functional male gametes, used to avoid hand emasculation
the mating of a crop with a distantly related wild species to bring in new characters
items.s: Wide crossing: the mating of a crop with a distantly related wild species to bring in new characters. The other options describe Tolerance, Male sterility, Emasculation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the picking of individual plants on appearance and the bulking of their produce for the next generation”?
o: Mass selection
Progeny test
Roguing
Marker-assisted choice
items.s: Mass selection is the picking of individual plants on appearance and the bulking of their produce for the next generation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Cytoplasmic male sterility?
o: a structural change such as a deletion, duplication, inversion or exchange within the set
the whole stock of hereditary material, held as seed, plants or tissue, available for use in a programme
a standard character recorded for every sample so that entries in a collection can be compared
a condition inherited through the maternal parent that prevents viable gamete formation
items.s: Cytoplasmic male sterility: a condition inherited through the maternal parent that prevents viable gamete formation. The other options describe Chromosome aberration, Germplasm, Descriptor.

items.q: All of the following belong to Mutation, polyploidy and chromosome manipulation EXCEPT
o: Trait
Trisomic
Chromosome doubling
Haploid
items.s: Every other option belongs to Mutation, polyploidy and chromosome manipulation. “Trait” belongs to Scope, aims and history of crop improvement, not Mutation, polyploidy and chromosome manipulation.

items.q: Pleiotropy may be defined as
o: the growing of a segregating stand for several generations with no individual choice until strains are fixed
the artificial duplication of the whole chromosome set of a cell, commonly with an alkaloid treatment
the transfer of male gametes from anther to stigma within the same flower or the same individual
the control of several different characters by a single hereditary unit
items.s: Pleiotropy: the control of several different characters by a single hereditary unit. The other options describe Chromosome doubling, Self-pollination, Bulk population method.
items.t: Inheritance of qualitative and quantitative traits

items.q: Participatory evaluation may be defined as
o: the repetition of a chromosome segment, giving extra copies of the units it carries
the failure of a plant to shed functional male gametes, used to avoid hand emasculation
the joint scoring of candidate material by researchers and farming households in their own fields
a planting of approved stock managed to produce large quantities of propagating material
items.s: Participatory evaluation: the joint scoring of candidate material by researchers and farming households in their own fields. The other options describe Duplication, Increase plot, Male sterility.

items.q: The statement “a distinct sample of planting material entered in a collection under one number” describes which of the following?
o: Accession
Protoplast fusion
Tissue culture
Ex situ conservation
items.s: Accession is a distinct sample of planting material entered in a collection under one number.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Top cross?
o: an individual whose extra chromosome sets all come from a single species
the offspring of an inbred parent mated to a broad-based tester population
repeated cycles of intercrossing and choice used to raise the frequency of favourable alleles in a stand
a farmer-maintained population long adapted to a locality through many seasons of on-farm choice
items.s: Top cross: the offspring of an inbred parent mated to a broad-based tester population. The other options describe Landrace, Autopolyploid, Recurrent selection.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Cleistogamy?
o: the location of a chromosome region governing a measured character by linking inherited differences to performance
the condition in which a flower sets seed without ever opening its petals
a planting of approved stock managed to produce large quantities of propagating material
the growing out of stored material to obtain fresh viable samples before vigour is lost
items.s: Cleistogamy: the condition in which a flower sets seed without ever opening its petals. The other options describe Locus mapping, Increase plot, Regeneration.
items.t: Reproductive systems and their breeding consequences

items.q: Tolerance may be defined as
o: a nearly homozygous strain built up by several generations of selfing
the joint scoring of candidate material by researchers and farming households in their own fields
the ability to lose less yield than a susceptible plant under the same level of attack
the transfer of male gametes from anther to stigma within the same flower or the same individual
items.s: Tolerance: the ability to lose less yield than a susceptible plant under the same level of attack. The other options describe Participatory evaluation, Self-pollination, Inbred line.
items.t: Breeding for disease, pest and stress resistance

items.q: Which of the following best describes Trait?
o: a measurable characteristic of an organism such as height, earliness or reaction to an attacker
the set of characters that allow an acceptable harvest where moisture is short
the presence of an abnormal number of single chromosomes, such as one too few
a farmer-maintained population long adapted to a locality through many seasons of on-farm choice
items.s: Trait: a measurable characteristic of an organism such as height, earliness or reaction to an attacker. The other options describe Landrace, Drought adaptation, Aneuploidy.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Landrace may be defined as
o: the keeping of samples away from their place of origin in cold stores or field collections
the hereditary constitution of an individual, whether considered at one locus or throughout
protection that works against some strains of an attacker but not against others
a farmer-maintained population long adapted to a locality through many seasons of on-farm choice
items.s: Landrace: a farmer-maintained population long adapted to a locality through many seasons of on-farm choice. The other options describe Ex situ conservation, Vertical resistance, Genotype.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Doubled haploid may be defined as
o: the formal approval that allows a new strain to be multiplied and offered for sale
an individual carrying a single set of unpaired chromosomes
a fully homozygous line obtained by duplicating the chromosome set of a gamete-derived plantlet
the small stock held by the originating institution from which all further multiplication begins
items.s: Doubled haploid: a fully homozygous line obtained by duplicating the chromosome set of a gamete-derived plantlet. The other options describe Haploid, Breeder seed, Release.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Breeder seed.
o: the systematic keeping of parentage records for every generation descended from a cross
an individual whose chromosome sets come from two or more different species
a replicated field comparison of candidate entries grown together under one management
the small stock held by the originating institution from which all further multiplication begins
items.s: Breeder seed: the small stock held by the originating institution from which all further multiplication begins. The other options describe Allopolyploid, Variety trial, Pedigree method.
items.t: Field trials, registration and seed classes

items.q: The statement “a nearly homozygous strain built up by several generations of selfing” describes which of the following?
o: Hybridisation
Inbred line
Top cross
Cytoplasmic male sterility
items.s: Inbred line is a nearly homozygous strain built up by several generations of selfing.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Phenotype?
o: the offspring of an inbred parent mated to a broad-based tester population
the visible form and performance of an individual, set by its constitution together with its surroundings
the treatment of material with a physical or chemical agent to raise the frequency of heritable alteration
the masking of the effect of one allele by the other member of the pair at a locus
items.s: Phenotype: the visible form and performance of an individual, set by its constitution together with its surroundings. The other options describe Top cross, Dominance, Induced mutagenesis.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Synthetic variety may be defined as
o: a planting of a single entry across a whole site to measure how much the ground itself varies
the condition in which male and female flowers are borne on separate individuals
a population formed by intercrossing a set of chosen lines and multiplied from open pollination
a subgroup of an attacker with a distinct pattern of adaptation to host types
items.s: Synthetic variety: a population formed by intercrossing a set of chosen lines and multiplied from open pollination. The other options describe Biotype, Blank trial, Dioecy.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Phenotype?
o: a standard character recorded for every sample so that entries in a collection can be compared
the visible form and performance of an individual, set by its constitution together with its surroundings
a fully homozygous line obtained by duplicating the chromosome set of a gamete-derived plantlet
a feature governed by many hereditary units and expressed as a continuous range of values
items.s: Phenotype: the visible form and performance of an individual, set by its constitution together with its surroundings. The other options describe Quantitative character, Descriptor, Doubled haploid.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Recurrent selection.
o: repeated cycles of intercrossing and choice used to raise the frequency of favourable alleles in a stand
the enclosure of a flower head in a paper or cloth sleeve to keep out foreign male gametes
the masking of the effect of one allele by the other member of the pair at a locus
a hereditary mechanism that blocks fertilisation by gametes from the same plant
items.s: Recurrent selection: repeated cycles of intercrossing and choice used to raise the frequency of favourable alleles in a stand. The other options describe Dominance, Self-incompatibility, Bagging.

items.q: All of the following belong to Sources of genetic variation EXCEPT
o: Crossing over
Point change
Recombination
Environmental variance
items.s: Every other option belongs to Sources of genetic variation. “Environmental variance” belongs to Inheritance of qualitative and quantitative traits, not Sources of genetic variation.

items.q: The statement “the superiority of first generation offspring over the mean of their two parents” describes which of the following?
o: Heterosis
Emasculation
Top cross
Single cross
items.s: Heterosis is the superiority of first generation offspring over the mean of their two parents.

items.q: Which term is described by “the condition in which male and female flowers are borne on separate individuals”?
o: Protandry
Cleistogamy
Dioecy
Cross-pollination
items.s: Dioecy is the condition in which male and female flowers are borne on separate individuals.
items.t: Reproductive systems and their breeding consequences

items.q: Which of the following best describes Selection index?
o: the reversal of the order of a chromosome segment so that its units are re-arranged
a weighted score that combines several characters to rank candidates for retention
the portion of total variation in a population that is due to differences in constitution
the ability of a strain of an attacker to overcome a particular host defence
items.s: Selection index: a weighted score that combines several characters to rank candidates for retention. The other options describe Genetic variance, Inversion, Virulence.

items.q: Heterosis may be defined as
o: a feature governed by many hereditary units and expressed as a continuous range of values
the superiority of first generation offspring over the mean of their two parents
the ability to lose less yield than a susceptible plant under the same level of attack
the joint scoring of candidate material by researchers and farming households in their own fields
items.s: Heterosis: the superiority of first generation offspring over the mean of their two parents. The other options describe Participatory evaluation, Quantitative character, Tolerance.

items.q: Which term is described by “the release of male gametes before the stigma of the same flower becomes receptive”?
o: Cross-pollination
Protandry
Self-incompatibility
Protogyny
items.s: Protandry is the release of male gametes before the stigma of the same flower becomes receptive.
items.t: Reproductive systems and their breeding consequences

items.q: Which of the following best describes Cleistogamy?
o: a store where planting material is kept under controlled conditions for long-term safekeeping
the release of male gametes before the stigma of the same flower becomes receptive
the condition in which a flower sets seed without ever opening its petals
the repeated mating of an offspring to one parent so as to recover that parent's type
items.s: Cleistogamy: the condition in which a flower sets seed without ever opening its petals. The other options describe Gene bank, Backcross, Protandry.
items.t: Reproductive systems and their breeding consequences

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Recombination?
o: the pairing of a host factor with a corresponding factor in the attacker that triggers defence
the reshuffling of parental alleles during meiosis to give new combinations in the offspring
the condition in which male and female flowers are borne on separate individuals
a limited set chosen to represent most of the variation held in a much larger assemblage
items.s: Recombination: the reshuffling of parental alleles during meiosis to give new combinations in the offspring. The other options describe Core subset, Recognition matching, Dioecy.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Colchicine?
o: the share of the total variation in a character that is transmitted to the offspring
a feature governed by many hereditary units and expressed as a continuous range of values
the reversal of the order of a chromosome segment so that its units are re-arranged
an alkaloid that arrests cell division so that the chromosome number of treated tissue is doubled
items.s: Colchicine: an alkaloid that arrests cell division so that the chromosome number of treated tissue is doubled. The other options describe Inversion, Quantitative character, Heritability.

items.q: The statement “the hereditary constitution of an individual, whether considered at one locus or throughout” describes which of the following?
o: Genotype
Gene bank
Germplasm
Phenotype
items.s: Genotype is the hereditary constitution of an individual, whether considered at one locus or throughout.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Which term is described by “a feature governed by one or a few hereditary units and falling into distinct classes”?
o: Additive effect
Qualitative character
Polygenic
Heritability
items.s: Qualitative character is a feature governed by one or a few hereditary units and falling into distinct classes.
items.t: Inheritance of qualitative and quantitative traits

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Epistasis.
o: the tendency of units on the same chromosome to be transmitted together
the ripening of the female part of a flower before the male part of the same flower
protection that works against some strains of an attacker but not against others
the interaction in which one locus suppresses the expression of another locus
items.s: Epistasis: the interaction in which one locus suppresses the expression of another locus. The other options describe Protogyny, Linkage, Vertical resistance.
items.t: Inheritance of qualitative and quantitative traits

items.q: Variety trial may be defined as
o: a replicated field comparison of candidate entries grown together under one management
a model plant form designed in advance to perform well in a stated environment and management
a planting of approved stock managed to produce large quantities of propagating material
a planting of a single entry across a whole site to measure how much the ground itself varies
items.s: Variety trial: a replicated field comparison of candidate entries grown together under one management. The other options describe Blank trial, Ideotype, Increase plot.
items.t: Field trials, registration and seed classes

items.q: Which term is described by “the official examination that a candidate is new, even in its characters and unchanged on multiplication”?
o: Blank trial
Increase plot
Check entry
Registration test
items.s: Registration test is the official examination that a candidate is new, even in its characters and unchanged on multiplication.
items.t: Field trials, registration and seed classes

items.q: Dominance may be defined as
o: the presence of an abnormal number of single chromosomes, such as one too few
the portion of total variation in a population that is due to differences in constitution
the growth of cells or organs on a sterile nutrient medium away from the whole plant
the masking of the effect of one allele by the other member of the pair at a locus
items.s: Dominance: the masking of the effect of one allele by the other member of the pair at a locus. The other options describe Genetic variance, Tissue culture, Aneuploidy.
items.t: Inheritance of qualitative and quantitative traits

items.q: Which of the following best describes Landrace?
o: the treatment of material with a physical or chemical agent to raise the frequency of heritable alteration
the condition in which a flower opens normally and admits male gametes from outside
a farmer-maintained population long adapted to a locality through many seasons of on-farm choice
the condition of carrying more than two complete sets of chromosomes
items.s: Landrace: a farmer-maintained population long adapted to a locality through many seasons of on-farm choice. The other options describe Chasmogamy, Polyploidy, Induced mutagenesis.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Backcross.
o: the pattern of a repeated sequence used to identify an individual or a strain
the first generation offspring of two inbred parents
the repeated mating of an offspring to one parent so as to recover that parent's type
the superiority of first generation offspring over the mean of their two parents
items.s: Backcross: the repeated mating of an offspring to one parent so as to recover that parent's type. The other options describe DNA fingerprinting, Single cross, Heterosis.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Anther culture.
o: the growing out of stored material to obtain fresh viable samples before vigour is lost
a detectable difference in DNA that is inherited and can be followed through crosses
a named group within a species that is distinct, even in its characters and unchanged on multiplication
the raising of plantlets from the male organ so that a single chromosome set is recovered
items.s: Anther culture: the raising of plantlets from the male organ so that a single chromosome set is recovered. The other options describe Cultivated variety, Regeneration, Molecular marker.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Release?
o: the systematic keeping of parentage records for every generation descended from a cross
the formal approval that allows a new strain to be multiplied and offered for sale
a standard character recorded for every sample so that entries in a collection can be compared
the growth of cells or organs on a sterile nutrient medium away from the whole plant
items.s: Release: the formal approval that allows a new strain to be multiplied and offered for sale. The other options describe Pedigree method, Tissue culture, Descriptor.
items.t: Field trials, registration and seed classes

items.q: The statement “the whole stock of hereditary material, held as seed, plants or tissue, available for use in a programme” describes which of the following?
o: Phenotype
Cultivated variety
Ideotype
Germplasm
items.s: Germplasm is the whole stock of hereditary material, held as seed, plants or tissue, available for use in a programme.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Which term is described by “the mating of two genetically different parents so that their characters are combined”?
o: Synthetic variety
Male sterility
Hybridisation
Inbred line
items.s: Hybridisation is the mating of two genetically different parents so that their characters are combined.

items.q: Which term is described by “the visible form and performance of an individual, set by its constitution together with its surroundings”?
o: Crop improvement
Landrace
Phenotype
Cultivated variety
items.s: Phenotype is the visible form and performance of an individual, set by its constitution together with its surroundings.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: Breeder seed may be defined as
o: the joining of two cells stripped of their walls so that their contents are combined
the small stock held by the originating institution from which all further multiplication begins
a measurable characteristic of an organism such as height, earliness or reaction to an attacker
the portion of total variation in a population that is due to differences in growing conditions
items.s: Breeder seed: the small stock held by the originating institution from which all further multiplication begins. The other options describe Environmental variance, Protoplast fusion, Trait.
items.t: Field trials, registration and seed classes

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Linkage.
o: the sterile culture of an immature hybrid embryo that would otherwise abort
the allocation of entries to plots by chance so that no systematic bias enters
the tendency of units on the same chromosome to be transmitted together
an alkaloid that arrests cell division so that the chromosome number of treated tissue is doubled
items.s: Linkage: the tendency of units on the same chromosome to be transmitted together. The other options describe Randomisation, Colchicine, Embryo rescue.
items.t: Inheritance of qualitative and quantitative traits

items.q: Which of the following best describes Trisomic?
o: the exchange of segments between paired chromosomes during the first meiotic division
an individual carrying three copies of one chromosome while the rest are in pairs
a distinct sample of planting material entered in a collection under one number
repeated cycles of intercrossing and choice used to raise the frequency of favourable alleles in a stand
items.s: Trisomic: an individual carrying three copies of one chromosome while the rest are in pairs. The other options describe Crossing over, Accession, Recurrent selection.

items.q: Genetic erosion may be defined as
o: the loss of variation from farmers' fields as older populations are replaced by a few modern types
the allocation of entries to plots by chance so that no systematic bias enters
the judging of a parent by the performance of its offspring
a planting of approved stock managed to produce large quantities of propagating material
items.s: Genetic erosion: the loss of variation from farmers' fields as older populations are replaced by a few modern types. The other options describe Increase plot, Randomisation, Progeny test.

items.q: Tissue culture may be defined as
o: a hereditary mechanism that blocks fertilisation by gametes from the same plant
the share of the total variation in a character that is transmitted to the offspring
a fully homozygous line obtained by duplicating the chromosome set of a gamete-derived plantlet
the growth of cells or organs on a sterile nutrient medium away from the whole plant
items.s: Tissue culture: the growth of cells or organs on a sterile nutrient medium away from the whole plant. The other options describe Heritability, Self-incompatibility, Doubled haploid.

items.q: The statement “a standard included in every block to give a basis for judging newcomers” describes which of the following?
o: Increase plot
Registration test
Check entry
Breeder seed
items.s: Check entry is a standard included in every block to give a basis for judging newcomers.
items.t: Field trials, registration and seed classes

items.q: Which term is described by “the reversal of the order of a chromosome segment so that its units are re-arranged”?
o: Inversion
Chromosome doubling
Anther culture
Duplication
items.s: Inversion is the reversal of the order of a chromosome segment so that its units are re-arranged.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Induced mutagenesis?
o: the judging of a parent by the performance of its offspring
the joint scoring of candidate material by researchers and farming households in their own fields
the treatment of material with a physical or chemical agent to raise the frequency of heritable alteration
the extent to which a lot represents the intended constitution without admixture
items.s: Induced mutagenesis: the treatment of material with a physical or chemical agent to raise the frequency of heritable alteration. The other options describe Progeny test, Genetic purity, Participatory evaluation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pure line method?
o: the portion of total variation in a population that is due to differences in constitution
the ability of a strain of an attacker to overcome a particular host defence
the isolation of uniform offspring from one selfed individual and its increase as a distinct strain
the formal approval that allows a new strain to be multiplied and offered for sale
items.s: Pure line method: the isolation of uniform offspring from one selfed individual and its increase as a distinct strain. The other options describe Genetic variance, Virulence, Release.

items.q: Embryo rescue may be defined as
o: an individual whose chromosome sets come from two or more different species
the sterile culture of an immature hybrid embryo that would otherwise abort
a detectable difference in DNA that is inherited and can be followed through crosses
the portion of total variation in a population that is due to differences in constitution
items.s: Embryo rescue: the sterile culture of an immature hybrid embryo that would otherwise abort. The other options describe Allopolyploid, Molecular marker, Genetic variance.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Embryo rescue?
o: the masking of the effect of one allele by the other member of the pair at a locus
protection spread fairly evenly against every strain of an attacker
the sterile culture of an immature hybrid embryo that would otherwise abort
the heritable differences that appear among plantlets regenerated from cultured tissue
items.s: Embryo rescue: the sterile culture of an immature hybrid embryo that would otherwise abort. The other options describe Dominance, Horizontal resistance, Somaclonal variation.

items.q: Which term is described by “a planting of a single entry across a whole site to measure how much the ground itself varies”?
o: Increase plot
Release
Genetic purity
Blank trial
items.s: Blank trial is a planting of a single entry across a whole site to measure how much the ground itself varies.

o: Landrace
Qualitative character
Cultivated variety
Crop improvement

the interaction in which one locus suppresses the expression of another locus
the share of the total variation in a character that is transmitted to the offspring
items.s: Single seed descent: the advance of each generation through one propagule per plant until full homozygosity is reached. The other options describe Embryo rescue, Epistasis, Heritability.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Escape.
o: the growing of each entry more than once in a trial so that experimental error can be measured
the avoidance of attack through a difference in timing or habit rather than internal defence
the condition in which a flower sets seed without ever opening its petals
the share of the total variation in a character that is transmitted to the offspring

Male sterility
Inbreeding depression

the systematic keeping of parentage records for every generation descended from a cross

items.s: Descriptor: a standard character recorded for every sample so that entries in a collection can be compared. The other options describe Bagging, Pedigree method, Cleistogamy.

o: Dominance

Qualitative character

an alkaloid that arrests cell division so that the chromosome number of treated tissue is doubled
the enclosure of a flower head in a paper or cloth sleeve to keep out foreign male gametes
items.s: Bagging: the enclosure of a flower head in a paper or cloth sleeve to keep out foreign male gametes. The other options describe Environmental variance, Breeder seed, Colchicine.

protection that works against some strains of an attacker but not against others
the deliberate placing of an attacker or its propagules on material being tested
items.s: Vertical resistance: protection that works against some strains of an attacker but not against others. The other options describe Horizontal resistance, Inoculation, Recognition matching.

items.q: The correct meaning of Cultivated variety is
o: a named group within a species that is distinct, even in its characters and unchanged on multiplication
the whole stock of hereditary material, held as seed, plants or tissue, available for use in a programme
a farmer-maintained population long adapted to a locality through many seasons of on-farm choice
the visible form and performance of an individual, set by its constitution together with its surroundings
items.s: Cultivated variety: a named group within a species that is distinct, even in its characters and unchanged on multiplication. The other options describe Germplasm, Phenotype, Landrace.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: The correct meaning of Trait is
o: a store where planting material is kept under controlled conditions for long-term safekeeping
a measurable characteristic of an organism such as height, earliness or reaction to an attacker
the whole stock of hereditary material, held as seed, plants or tissue, available for use in a programme
a named group within a species that is distinct, even in its characters and unchanged on multiplication
items.s: Trait: a measurable characteristic of an organism such as height, earliness or reaction to an attacker. The other options describe Cultivated variety, Gene bank, Germplasm.
items.t: Scope, aims and history of crop improvement

items.q: The correct meaning of Epistasis is
o: a feature governed by one or a few hereditary units and falling into distinct classes
the portion of total variation in a population that is due to differences in constitution
the portion of total variation in a population that is due to differences in growing conditions
the interaction in which one locus suppresses the expression of another locus
items.s: Epistasis: the interaction in which one locus suppresses the expression of another locus. The other options describe Genetic variance, Environmental variance, Qualitative character.
items.t: Inheritance of qualitative and quantitative traits

items.q: The correct meaning of Recombination is
o: the heritable differences that appear among plantlets regenerated from cultured tissue
the mating of a crop with a distantly related wild species to bring in new characters
the reshuffling of parental alleles during meiosis to give new combinations in the offspring
the presence of an abnormal number of single chromosomes, such as one too few
items.s: Recombination: the reshuffling of parental alleles during meiosis to give new combinations in the offspring. The other options describe Wide crossing, Somaclonal variation, Aneuploidy.

items.q: The correct meaning of Chromosome doubling is
o: the raising of plantlets from the male organ so that a single chromosome set is recovered
the artificial duplication of the whole chromosome set of a cell, commonly with an alkaloid treatment
the repetition of a chromosome segment, giving extra copies of the units it carries
the sterile culture of an immature hybrid embryo that would otherwise abort
items.s: Chromosome doubling: the artificial duplication of the whole chromosome set of a cell, commonly with an alkaloid treatment. The other options describe Duplication, Embryo rescue, Anther culture.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Dominance.
o: the portion of total variation in a population that is due to differences in constitution
the share of the total variation in a character that is transmitted to the offspring
the masking of the effect of one allele by the other member of the pair at a locus
governed by several hereditary units each contributing a small part of the total effect
items.s: Dominance: the masking of the effect of one allele by the other member of the pair at a locus. The other options describe Polygenic, Heritability, Genetic variance.
items.t: Inheritance of qualitative and quantitative traits

items.q: Single cross may be defined as
o: the superiority of first generation offspring over the mean of their two parents
a condition inherited through the maternal parent that prevents viable gamete formation
the mating of two genetically different parents so that their characters are combined
the first generation offspring of two inbred parents
items.s: Single cross: the first generation offspring of two inbred parents. The other options describe Hybridisation, Heterosis, Cytoplasmic male sterility.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an individual carrying three copies of one chromosome while the rest are in pairs”
o: Trisomic
Haploid
Chromosome aberration
Chromosome doubling
items.s: Trisomic is an individual carrying three copies of one chromosome while the rest are in pairs.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Registration test?
o: the official examination that a candidate is new, even in its characters and unchanged on multiplication
the small stock held by the originating institution from which all further multiplication begins
the allocation of entries to plots by chance so that no systematic bias enters
the extent to which a lot represents the intended constitution without admixture
items.s: Registration test: the official examination that a candidate is new, even in its characters and unchanged on multiplication. The other options describe Genetic purity, Breeder seed, Randomisation.
items.t: Field trials, registration and seed classes

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Micropropagation.
o: the joining of two cells stripped of their walls so that their contents are combined
the rapid multiplication of plantlets from small tissue pieces in sterile culture
the precise alteration of a chosen sequence within a living genome
the pattern of a repeated sequence used to identify an individual or a strain
items.s: Micropropagation: the rapid multiplication of plantlets from small tissue pieces in sterile culture. The other options describe DNA fingerprinting, Protoplast fusion, Gene editing.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the transfer of male gametes between separate individuals of a species”

Monoecy
Cleistogamy
Dioecy

the mating of a crop with a distantly related wild species to bring in new characters
the condition of carrying more than two complete sets of chromosomes
the treatment of material with a physical or chemical agent to raise the frequency of heritable alteration
items.s: Induced mutagenesis: the treatment of material with a physical or chemical agent to raise the frequency of heritable alteration. The other options describe Aneuploidy, Polyploidy, Wide crossing.

items.q: In this course, Self-incompatibility refers to

a hereditary mechanism that blocks fertilisation by gametes from the same plant
the transfer of male gametes from anther to stigma within the same flower or the same individual
the formation of viable seed without fertilisation, giving progeny identical to the mother plant

items.t: Reproductive systems and their breeding consequences

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pedigree method?
o: the removal of off-types and diseased individuals from a multiplying stand
the systematic keeping of parentage records for every generation descended from a cross
the picking of individual plants on appearance and the bulking of their produce for the next generation
the repeated mating of an offspring to one parent so as to recover that parent's type
items.s: Pedigree method: the systematic keeping of parentage records for every generation descended from a cross. The other options describe Roguing, Backcross, Mass selection.

Monoecy
Protandry
Cleistogamy

items.t: Reproductive systems and their breeding consequences

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Core subset.

the keeping of samples away from their place of origin in cold stores or field collections
a distinct sample of planting material entered in a collection under one number
a hereditary unit moved from one organism into another by artificial means
items.s: Core subset: a limited set chosen to represent most of the variation held in a much larger assemblage. The other options describe Transgene, Ex situ conservation, Accession.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the removal of anthers from a flower before they shed so that only a chosen parent fertilises it”

Emasculation
Top cross

Check entry
Release
Replication

items.q: Gene editing may be defined as

the precise alteration of a chosen sequence within a living genome
the joint scoring of candidate material by researchers and farming households in their own fields
a standard character recorded for every sample so that entries in a collection can be compared
